thread.title: UW-Green Bay to honor student civic engagement and community partnerships on May 8
thread.title_full: UW-Green Bay to honor student civic engagement and community partnerships on May 8

author: The Sconi
title: UW-Green Bay to honor student civic engagement and community partnerships on May 8
text:
The University of Wisconsin–Green Bay will celebrate student leadership and community collaboration during its Celebrating Civic Engagement event, scheduled for May 8 at The Mauthe Center on campus. The event brings together students, faculty, nonprofit leaders, and civic partners to recognize the impact of hands-on learning and regional partnerships in Northeast Wisconsin.
The university said the gathering highlights how experiential education is preparing students for civic leadership roles. Ashley Heath, director of UW–Green Bay’s Center for Civic Engagement and assistant teaching professor in Public and Environmental Affairs, said, “At UW–Green Bay, civic engagement is experiential and student‑driven. Our students are gaining real‑world experience by working directly with community partners on challenges facing our region, learning first-hand the impact their efforts have in the community.”
Honorees include participants from the Civic Scholars Leadership Program cohort, Spring Community Impact Practicum members, Newman Civic Fellows from UW–Green Bay, as well as this year’s Community Partner of the Year. Students enrolled in a Strategic Philanthropy course will also announce the recipient of this year’s Giving Circle grant.
The Civic Scholars Leadership Program offers a year-long interdisciplinary experience open to all majors through site visits and projects that build connections between students and local communities. This spring’s Community Impact Practicum partnered with House of Hope in Green Bay; students worked as a team on organization-identified projects supporting operations and outreach efforts.
Program growth has been supported by a $75,000 two-year grant from Herb Kohl Philanthropies that expands opportunities for student leadership through transportation support, mentorships, and programming. For many participants like Cooper Laper—a political science major considering law school—the experience shapes career paths: “I was unsure about what kind of law I wanted to practice,” said Laper. “But after engaging with more disenfranchised groups and seeing things as they are in the community, [this] inspired me to want to follow that path and help people who really need it.”
The university describes itself as serving over 11,500 undergraduate through doctoral students annually across several campus locations in Northeast Wisconsin; it provides access to more than 200 academic options including majors, minors, certificates or programs according to the official website . The school emphasizes resilience—its athletic teams use Phoenix as their nickname—and focuses on regional care while promoting diversity through educational inclusivity initiatives according to the official website .
University officials say events like Celebrating Civic Engagement reflect an ongoing commitment to building civic leaders who contribute positively both today and into the future.
